result:
**Recommendation: one candidate survives the audit. Sub-center ArcFace at the fit-product classifier layer, falsified first on the existing cached fit-inner CPU format with a sham-assignment control.** No edits, jobs, or consultations were made. The ledger audit and the new measurement it rests on are below, with measurement and conjecture kept apart.

## What the new terminal evidence says, and what it does not

**Measured.** The direct256 arm shows the width advantage decaying with training, from +0.80 pp at 100 updates to +0.24 pp at 1000, with only 40 rescues against 25 regressions. Every closed objective-side arm on this recipe moved held R@1 by less than ±0.3 pp: specific-impostor hinge (−0.02 pp), worst-positive hinge (killed), valid-anchor, mAP-aligned, teacher transfer, head-first warm-up, gradient projection, repeat coverage, fit-product scaling (+0.37 pp). So on this fixed budget, the 128-dimensional head is not the binding layer at convergence, and reweighting which *pairs* get gradient is not either.

**Not measured.** Fit-set best-positive Recall@1 for the current checkpoint is not recorded anywhere in the lane. The 99.36% figure belongs to the older 23,342-image model. So a fit-versus-held generalization gap cannot be asserted, and parameter-space regularizers (L2-SP, sharpness-aware minimization, soups) have no fit-side causal signal to point to. Their prior mentions are all in the August UNICOM proposal lanes, not verdicts on this recipe.

## The one fit-only signal that is new

The fit-positive-tail receipt (seed 179026, 1000 updates, 13,271 eligible fit anchors, worst-positive margins) has never been stratified by product structure. I did that with stdlib only, joining the receipt's query ordinals to the pinned partition replay at `/tmp/sfora-inshop-partition-replay.txt`. The partition hash was not re-asserted in my census because that assertion sat behind a numpy import that this box lacks. The file is the one the archived verifiers read.

Tail means a different-product image scores above the anchor's worst same-product image by more than 0.03. Series is the filename's first token, the same "acquisition group" the ledger's helper parses.

| Product size × series count | Eligible anchors | Tail rate | Median margin |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| ≤4 images, 1 series | 3,862 | 0.3–1.0% | −0.24 to −0.29 |
| 5–6 images, 1 series | 1,668 | 3.6–11% | −0.16 to −0.18 |
| 7–8 images, 2 series | 1,902 | 8–12% | −0.12 to −0.14 |
| 9–10 images, 2 series | 1,057 | 18–20% | −0.06 to −0.08 |
| 10+ images, ≥3 series | 4,471 | **44.3%** | **−0.001** |

Pose is not the driver: tail rates by pose are 16–22% for every pose except the tiny `flat` class. All 356 fit products with 9 or more images are multi-series, and held products have the same series composition (1,362 single-series, 400 two-series, 135 three-series). The `flat`-only census and the by-pose table were also computed.

**Measured conclusion.** At the end of the fixed 64,000-presentation budget, the unresolved fit rank structure is concentrated almost entirely in multi-series products, where the median anchor has a negative sitting at its worst positive. A third of the fit anchors live in this stratum.

**Conjecture, not measured.** The single class proxy per product in `sharded_mask_arcface_loss` (margin 0.3, scale 64, one proxy per 2,004 products, class-mean initialized) is the term that pulls all series of a product to one center. On a fixed budget, that gradient is spent on cross-series compression of large fit products, and it shapes the upper 12 blocks toward series-collapsing features that unseen products do not benefit from. The bank SmoothAP term keeps all same-product images as ranked positives either way, so the deployed positive semantics and the mAP@R target are untouched.

## Why this is causally distinct from the closed ledger

- The worst-positive hinge (killed) and repeat-coverage (killed) *added* pressure on exactly these anchors. This candidate *removes* a competing pull instead. Opposite sign, different layer (classifier geometry, not pair weighting or sampling).
- The acquisition-group held lane was killed because only 10 of 151 held misses lack a same-series positive. That kills "learn cross-series retrieval" as the mechanism. It does not test this one, whose claimed path is freed budget and less distorted geometry, not cross-series recall. The held misses are 44% close-margin same-series confusions, which is what freed budget would have to fix. That link is the conjecture the falsifier tests.
- Proxy Synthesis, asymmetric proxy, centroid-PCA, and live-head bank changed proxy *initialization*, *virtual classes*, or bank freshness, not the number of centers a real class may occupy.
- The only prior sub-center verdict in the repository is sub-center Proxy Anchor on the July substrate, recorded as a Gate 2 failure at `docs/method_search_verdict.md:533` (0.675 vs 0.695). That is a real negative for a different loss, backbone, and data regime. It is not evidence about ArcFace on SigLIP2 with this budget, and it should be cited as a caution in the freeze, not as closure.

## The mechanism and the minimal hook

Sub-center ArcFace, Deng, Guo, Liu, Gong, Zafeiriou, ECCV 2020, arXiv 2010.05350. Each class holds K proxies. The class logit is the maximum cosine over its K sub-centers; margin and cross-entropy are applied to that logit. Only the nearest sub-center receives the pull. The paper's own caveat applies and must be in the freeze: on clean single-modal data K>1 slightly *hurt* until non-dominant sub-centers were dropped. Here the multi-modality is real colour or series variation, which is the case the method was built for.

Hook, all training-only, serving untouched:

- `src/sfora/unicom_training.py` `sharded_mask_arcface_logits`: accept `subcenters: int = 1`; the weight tensor becomes `(C·K, D)`; after the shard concatenation, `logits.view(B, C, K).amax(-1)` before the existing margin and clamp.
- `scripts/train_inshop_siglip2_unseen_gallery.py` around line 931: replicate the class-mean proxy K times with a small deterministic jitter so the sub-centers can separate. Classifier grows from 2,004×128 to 6,012×128. Nothing else in the loss, bank, schedule, optimizer, freeze, PCA head, or scorer changes.

## Cheapest bounded falsifier before any GPU work

Use the existing cached fit-inner CPU format already used by head-first and repeat-coverage F1: pinned pretrained fit cache, fit-inner split (6,757 fit images, 995 products; 3,440 query, 3,074 gallery on 997 disjoint validation products), same head, bank, schedule, packed scorer. Three arms:

1. **Native**, K=1.
2. **Treatment**, K=3, nearest-sub-center assignment.
3. **Sham**, K=3 with a fixed random sub-center assigned to each fit image at start. Same parameter count and initialization, no adaptive modality selection. This separates "more proxies" from "the class may occupy several centers."

Predeclare before running:

- Mechanism signal on fit only: among multi-series fit products, the fraction whose images occupy at least two sub-centers, and the series purity of that occupancy, must exceed the sham arm's values. If treatment assignments do not split multi-series products better than random, the mechanism is absent. Kill.
- Quality on the inner validation, packed scorer: treatment minus native R@1 at least +0.5 pp with paired product-bootstrap lower bound above zero, mAP@R not below native minus 0.002, and sham minus native inside its own interval. These reuse the lane's existing effect-size floors rather than a new number.
- Cost guard: CPU wall within 1.10× of native.

A pass authorizes only one frozen paired 100-update GPU arm on seed 179024 under the same +0.5 pp and +0.01 floors the direct256 arm just failed, then the standard 1000-update confirmation. A fail closes the classifier-geometry layer for this recipe. The cached-head regime sits near 87% and is not the encoder regime, so a cached pass is a mechanism result, not a quality forecast.

## What I could not do here

No numpy exists on this box and downloads are prohibited, so I did not rescore the saved held tensors locally. Two cheap fit-side reads that would sharpen the freeze remain undone: the current checkpoint's fit best-positive Recall@1, and for each tail anchor whether its worst positive lies in a different series. Both are computable on the DGX from the retained seed-179026 fit export in well under a minute of CPU. Neither is required to run the cached falsifier above.
